claims.text: For the 20 November 2025 election, IPU's Candidates field reads 'Not applicable. There is no party system or candidates stood as independents.' Its 'Number of parties winning seats', 'Percentage of parties winning seats' and 'Percentage of seats won by largest party or coalition' fields also read 'Not applicable'. The 'About the election' narrative names no party and does not mention PTOA or DPFI.
claims.locator: Background, 'Candidates'; Results, 'About the election' and the three party fields
claims.uncertainty: IPU's silence states neither that PTOA won no seats nor that it won any; it supports only that IPU records no party-level result for 2025.

claims.text: IPU's page for the November 2025 election states that in December 2024 Prime Minister Siaosi Sovaleni resigned ahead of a vote of confidence, that former long-serving finance minister 'Aisake Eke succeeded him in January 2025, and that in the same month King Tupou VI appointed Crown Prince Tupouto'a 'Ulukalala Minister for Foreign Affairs and Minister for His Majesty's Armed Forces.
claims.uncertainty: Secondary international database with month precision; corroboration only. 'Vote of confidence' is as printed; the Assembly records call it a motion of no confidence.

scope_note: Live Parline page read after the cutoff for its 2025 election-description fields (CLAUDE-C01-04) and its dated December 2024 to January 2025 narrative (CLAUDE-C01-03) only; the page shows no revision date, and no other November 2025 election content is imported. IPU cites Legislative Assembly communications of 23 November 2025 and 23 January 2026 and news outlets. A direct non-browser request returned HTTP 403.
